newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian brewery bucks trend on sluggish bourse.
newsitem.headline: Croatian brewery bucks trend on sluggish bourse.

text.p: Brewery Karlovacka Pivovara took centre stage on the Zagreb bourse on Tuesday, closing 14 percent higher at 570 kuna, while most other stocks were unchanged or closed lower in sluggish trade.

Karlovacka was also the most actively traded issue, selling 2,120 shares. Most of it, a package of 2,000 shares, was sold for 520 kuna in what seemed like a pre-arranged deal and the rest for 530 and 570 kuna.
"The average price was around 540 kuna and I expect the trade tomorrow to start from there," said Zoran Ilic of Counsult Invest, who predicted last week the price would go as high as 600 kuna.
The buying orders for Karlovacka overshot selling orders by 70 to one on Tuesday, supporting the view of many traders that the stock would continue rising.
"Everything that was on offer was sold," one trader said.
Analysts at another brokerage, I.C.F., put Karlovacka's actual book value at 773 kuna per share and its price/earnings ratio at 7.1, giving it a strong "buy" recommendation.
Karlovacka brewery, in which the majority stake is controlled by Chilean Cervecerias Unidas, has been the market's darling in recent days, growing steadily from around 360 kuna two weeks ago.
Market participants linked its strong growth to a discrepancy between the share price which was viewed as low and positive 1996 results.
But prospects for other shares were not so rosy ahead of the traditional summer lull, and traders said this could be the last week of relatively active trading on the Zagreb Bourse.
Of 16 issues seven fell, three rose and six were flat. Volume shrank by more than half to 8,527 from 18,694 units and turnover was also down to 4.8 million from 11.5 million kuna on Friday.
Among the losers, hotelier Suncani Hvar lost three kuna to close at 52, selling 121 shares. Laguna Porec inched down four kuna to 1,501 kuna on volume of 371 shares.
Food concern Podravka lost 13 kuna to 255, trading 1,216 shares, and traders said it could drop further as small shareholders embarked on a selling spree.
Of the blue chips, Zagrebacka Banka lost 50 kuna to close at 1,920, trading only 296 shares. Traders said this was a good price for Zagrebacka and it was likely to recover.
Pliva remained flat at 480 on meagre volume of 430 shares, and so did chocolate maker Kras at 430 kuna on volume of 1,037 shares.
